requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 acceptance of ICMP redirects on node1
requirements.summary: A persistent sysctl.d config (/etc/sysctl.d/99-network-hardening.conf) sets net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects, net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_redirects, and secure_redirects variants to 0. Live values confirmed at 0 both immediately after applying and after a full reboot, with the config file intact post-reboot, directly demonstrating persistence.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 acceptance of source-routed packets on node1
requirements.summary: The same sysctl.d config sets net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route and net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_source_route to 0 (default was 1 at baseline). Verified live at 0 after apply and again after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Change is persistent across restarts (not just live sysctl state)
requirements.summary: Executor performed a full reboot of node1, confirmed via a changed boot_id (a1dc8e25... -> bd906608...), consistent with the fixed lifecycle before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots. Post-reboot verification shows all six hardening keys remain 0 and the config file is intact, directly proving the settings survive a real restart rather than relying on configuration alone.

overall_summary: The executor persistently disabled IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance on node1 via a sysctl.d drop-in file, applied it live, and — going beyond the minimum requirement — validated true persistence by performing a full reboot and confirming both a changed boot identity and unchanged (still-disabled) hardening values afterward. This reboot also satisfies the separate provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol. All material task outcomes are directly and coherently evidenced.
limitations: No before_prepare/after_prepare distinction exists (prepare phase was not configured; after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare), so preparer-vs-executor state could not be separately isolated, though this does not affect scoring since the only meaningful change is executor-caused.

Per-interface (non-default) sysctl values were not individually checked, only the all/default aggregate keys; this is standard practice for system-wide hardening but interface-specific overrides, if any existed, were not explicitly ruled out.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: cmd-8e613955ec514212 captured baseline and wrote/applied the persistent sysctl config; cmd-d1ccac37f25b45ae scheduled the reboot required to demonstrate persistence (and satisfies the independent provider-wide restart-evidence protocol); the subsequent polling and verification commands were read-only. No unnecessary mutations, leftover temporary files, or failed services were introduced — the tmp-directory diff between before_prepare and after_executor reflects normal systemd-private directories tied to the old vs. new boot_id, an expected reboot artifact rather than executor residue. Failed-services and listening-sockets observations are empty in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, and package-health remained unchanged (dpkg, no reported issues).
